summary: David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna.

David Teplitz was an Indology scholar who earned an M.A. from Northwestern University and a Ph.D. from the American Academy of Asian Studies. He served as a teacher at the California Institute of Integral Studies.

David Tracy was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He taught at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (1969–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale universities. He was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1971–2000) and taught at Soka University of America in 2000.

David W. Tien is a scholar of Sinology and philosophy. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, working with Julia Ching, Robert H. Sharf, and doctoral supervisor James Robson.
David Webster is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD at the University of Bristol under the supervision of Peter Harvey.

David Zilberman was a philosopher and Indologist who studied under Yuri Levada (1968–1972). He held posts at Odesa University, the Odessa Hydrometeorological Institute, Hunter College (1973), the University of Chicago (1974), and Brandeis University (1976).

Davoud Monchi-Zadeh was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Walther Wüst, and held posts at the University of Munich (~1943–1945), Alexandria University (~1951–1952), and Uppsala University (~1953–1979).
Daw Ohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and linguistics who studied at the University of Rangoon and served there as a Tutor in Pali, attested in 1977.

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at St. Stephen's College, the University of Delhi, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at SFSU, USF, CIIS, and served as professor of Central Asian studies at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1987–2003).
Dawa Tsering is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle and at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies. He has held a post at Tibet University.
Dawei Wang is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Sichuan University and held an appointment at its Institute for Daoism and Religious Culture Studies.

Daya Krishna was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as professor of philosophy and Pro Vice-Chancellor at the University of Rajasthan (~1969–1984) and as chairman of the Indian Council of Philosophical Research (attested 1999).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University of the Punjab, Oriental College, and under John Marshall. He held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India (1925, 1931–1935) and directed archaeology in Jaipur State from 1935.

Dayananda Saraswati was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Sri Jayachamarajendra Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya and under teachers including P. S. Subramania Iyer, Veeraraghavachariar, Swami Pranavananda, Swami Tarananda Giri, Swami Tapovan Maharaj, and Virajanand Dandeesha.

Dayong was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Taixu, Paldan Tenzin Nyandrak, Bai Puren, and Dorje Geshe. He studied at and taught at the Wuchang Buddhist Institute in 1923.

Dean Anderson is an Indologist and historian who served as Director of the South and Central Asia Research Institute (attested 2003–2004) and held a post at the East West Cultural Institute (attested 2013–2017).
Debabrata Sensharma is an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Gopinath Kaviraj. He held a professorship at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture, attested in 2009.

Debala Mitra was an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Dineschandra Sircar. She served as Additional Director General at the Archaeological Survey of India from 1981 to 1983.
Debamitra Dey is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned a Bachelor of Arts in Sanskrit (1997–2000) and a Doctor of Philosophy (2003–2008) at Jadavpur University.
